trickyParts: The run lock is flock on $LOADTEST_ROOT/.run.lock (fd 9); the holder writes a random token into the file and exports it, so its own children (run-series.sh's run-step.sh, run-step.sh's stack.sh) pass while any other caller is refused; stack.sh closes fd 9 in every stack process it spawns so no daemon inherits the lock.
box_busy_before is read by run-step.sh before the reset (loadgen box-busy, passed as -box-busy-before): read after Dispatch starts it measured Dispatch's own start-up (23% on an idle box).

pg_blocking_pids takes exclusive access to the lock manager, and even without it the ungranted-lock query costs 75-180 ms of a Postgres backend per read at 1x; the sampler names blockers from its own pg_locks read and runs once a second.
deviations: Ported INFRA-591's samplers (ungranted_locks, sse, delivery_ms_from_sent, resources.xids_per_s) into this PR at INFRA-514's architect's instruction (Envoy, 09:40Z); not ported: the patch's _all/_first and from-response/from-created_at NATS delivery variants, which this package's arrival/commit/sent columns replace.

The ungranted-lock sampler reads once a second, not every 20 ms as in INFRA-591's patch, and its 'first blocker' is the lowest-pid granted holder of the same lock, not pg_blocking_pids[1]; INFRA-591's implementer was told its 20 ms measurements loaded Postgres.
discoveredComplexity: Committed rate at 1x on one build and seed varies 0.74-1.95 events/s across eight runs with box_busy_before <= 1%; /proc/stat sees only this pod, not other pods on the node. README asks for five or more runs per side and medians.
